eyebrow: Assigning a variable — no declaration needed
code:
fare_amount = 14.50
passenger_count = 1
vendor_id = "2"

# Python figures out the type from the VALUE itself.
# This is called dynamic typing.
caption: No type keyword, no upfront declaration — just a name, an equals sign, a value.

eyebrow: The five core types, with real taxi columns
code:
fare_amount = 14.50           # float -> fare_amount
passenger_count = 1           # int   -> passenger_count
vendor_id = "2"                # str   -> VendorID (yes, TEXT)
is_shared_ride = False         # bool
tip_amount = None              # NoneType -- genuinely missing
caption: int, float, str, bool, and None — you'll use every one of these constantly.
type() confirms what Python actually decided — useful the moment something behaves unexpectedly.

subtitle: Holding more than one value at a time.
